chapter: Art Hodes, Bechet and Blue Note
title: World War One draft: put in a cage as a supposed slacker
summary: In Birmingham he was displayed as a slacker, then found too young for the first war and too old for the second.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: So then, of course, the War is going on. Did you have any concerns about the War? You were say around 41 or 42 when the United States got involved in the War. But they were drafting these people up until about age 45, weren't they?

Yeah. I think during that time... I think I was in Birmingham, Alabama. What year it was, I don't know. It was round about... Anyway, I think I was around Birmingham. Eighteen or nineteen years old, somewhere
Moore (III) - 36
around there. But I wouldn't say I was arrested as a slacker. When that come about, I don't know. All I know is some guy comes at me, man, and put me...
Oh, World War One.
Oh that's World War...yeah... I don't know whether that's to scare (?) people or what it was. He put me in this thing that looked like a telephone booth.
Oh yeah, you were talking about that.
Yeah, a telephone booth...
It seemed like a cage.
Yeah, like a cage. It wasn't no iron, just a rubber thing that looked like the... What do you call them things keepin' burglars out? Iron bars.
Iron bars.
But they wasn't iron bars. It was just...
Hard rubber.
Yeah. Had me stand up in there, and people would pass by, look at me: "What you did?" "We got him for a slacker." But they found out I was too young for the first one and too old for the second one.
Too old for the second one.
Yeah. I think they did that mostly to perform(?). You know, to kind of scare the other people up. If someone didn't register or didn't sign up, he'd go on and
Moore (III) - 37
sign up, you know.
Sure.
I didn't know nothin' about no army, you know...
